AiUseDeclaration.description: The candidate's answer to "did you use AI tools to apply?".

AiUsePolicy.description: What the employer allows candidates to do with AI tools while applying.

AnswerFact.description: A candidate's answer to one question. A multiple-choice answer has one value per chosen option.

ApiMeta.description: What is serving this API: the product name, the build version and the hosting environment.

ApplicationDetail.description:
One application: the candidate, the job, where it is in the job's workflow, its tags, and the candidate's
declarations.

ApplicationStage.description: A stage of the job's workflow, as an application sees it.

ApplicationSummary.description:
An application in a list. No accommodation flag here: lists reach every reviewer, so it shows only on the
application itself.

ApplicationTaskEntry.description: Something a person should do about an application: a review, a to-do, or a rejection to decide on.

ApplicationTimelineEntry.description: One entry of an application's timeline, oldest first. Members that do not apply to the type are null.

Automation.description:
Trigger, conditions, actions (workflow-engine.md §2). Stored and validated structurally here; the workflow engine
runs them. DefinitionValidator refuses an automation that would reject anyone because of an integrity
signal (ADR-0004).

AutomationAction.description:
One action. Which optional members apply depends on ActionType AutomationAction.Type; DefinitionValidator checks
that each type has what it needs and nothing else.

AutomationCondition.description:
One test of an application fact, such as `answers.work_authorization EqualTo no` (yes/no answers are
`yes` and `no`, choice answers are option ids). Facts are
`answers.{questionId}`, `integrity.authenticity`, `integrity.aiAssistance`,
`verification.result`, `application.tags`, `application.source` and
`application.hoursInStage`.

AutomationConditions.description:
Conditions combined with ConditionMatch AutomationConditions.Match; a rule with bool AutomationCondition.Negate is a "not". One
level on purpose: a recursive tree would make the JSON Schema and the generated client recursive too.

AutomationFacts.description:
What an automation's conditions can see about one application at the moment its trigger fired: the facts snapshot
(docs/architecture/workflow-engine.md §3). The engine stores it with every run, so a replay or an audit sees exactly
what the conditions saw. A fact that is null or empty here is absent: ConditionOperator.Exists is false
and every other test fails.

AutomationIssue.description:
An automation that did not do its job: blocked (a loop, the depth limit, a workflow that no longer validates) or
failed (an action failed after its retries). Newest first; the run has the full record.

AutomationRunEntry.description:
The audit record of one automation evaluated for one application (workflow-engine.md §2, guardrail 3): the trigger,
the facts its conditions saw, which rules held, and what each action did.

CandidateDetail.description: A candidate and every application they made to the organization.

CandidateSummary.description: A candidate: one person per email address within the organization.

CreateApplicationRequest.description:
A recruiter adds an application by hand, for a candidate who applied another way. The candidate is matched by email
within the organization and created if new. The public apply flow is the careers site's.

CreateHiringTemplateRequest.description:
A new organization template, whose version 1 is a draft. Give a `definition`, or `copyFromVersionId` to
start from an existing version (a system template's, to customise it), or neither for a basic pipeline.

CreateHiringTemplateVersionRequest.description: Starts the next version as a draft: the given definition, or a copy of the newest version's.

CreateJobRequest.description:
A new job. With `templateVersionId` (a published version of an own or system template), the job copies that
version's workflow, and every field left out here takes the template's posting default. Without a slug, one is made
from the title.

CurrentOrganization.description: The organization the signed-in user works in, and their role there.

CurrentUser.description: The signed-in user, and the organization they work in (null until onboarding).

DefinitionError.description: A problem with a definition, at a JSON path such as `workflow.stages[1].id`.

HiringTemplateDefinition.description: A hiring template version's full definition: the workflow a job copies, plus defaults for the job's posting.

HiringTemplateDetail.description: A hiring template with its versions, oldest first.

HiringTemplateSummary.description: A hiring template in a list. System templates ship with the product and are read-only.

HiringTemplateVersionDetail.description:
One version of a hiring template with its full definition. The definition's JSON Schema is served at
`/v1/schemas/hiring-template-definition.json`.

HiringWorkflow.description:
What a hiring template versions and a job copies: the stage pipeline, the screening questionnaire, the integrity
policy and the automations.

IntegrityPolicy.description: The template's integrity settings (ADR-0004). Only the AI-use policy exists so far.

JobDetail.description: Everything about one job: posting content, lifecycle, its workflow copy and where that came from.

JobLocation.description:
A place the job is based: schema.org `PostalAddress` without the street. string? JobLocation.Country is an ISO 3166-1
alpha-2 code. The API requires it; a location carried over from the old free-text column may lack it.

JobSalary.description: A pay range. At least one of decimal? JobSalary.Min and decimal? JobSalary.Max is set; string JobSalary.Currency is ISO 4217.

JobSnapshot.description:
The posting content of a job at one moment: everything a careers page, a feed or a job board shows. A
JobVersion freezes one. Equality compares the content, list members included.

JobSummary.description: A job as shown in the recruiter dashboard's list.

JobTemplateDiff.description:
How the job's workflow differs from the newest published version of the template it came from. Empty
`changes` with `updateAvailable` false: the job is up to date.

JobTemplateSource.description: The template version a job's workflow was copied from, and whether a newer one is published.

JobVersionDetail.description: One published version of a job: the frozen content boards were sent.

JobVersionSummary.description: One published version of a job, without its content.

Knockout.description:
Marks a yes/no question as an objective eligibility check (work authorisation, a required licence). The answer
bool Knockout.DisqualifyingAnswer makes the candidate ineligible. It never rejects anyone by itself: an automation
decides, and by default it only queues the application for a person to review (workflow-engine.md §2).

MagicLinkRequest.description: Asks for a sign-in link by email.

MagicLinkVerification.description: Redeems the token from an emailed sign-in link.

ManualAutomationQueued.description: A manual automation was queued. `eventId` keys its run: find it in the application's automation runs.

MoveApplicationRequest.description: Moves an application to another stage of its job's workflow. Only people move applications here.

OnboardingRequest.description: Creates the signed-in user's organization, with them as its Owner.

PostingDefaults.description: Values a new job starts with when it is created from the template. Every member is optional.

PublicJob.description: A job as shown on a public careers page.

PublicJobBoard.description: The public careers listing for one organization.

Question.description:
One screening question. Which optional members apply depends on QuestionType Question.Type: IReadOnlyList<QuestionOption>? Question.Options for the
choice types, Knockout? Question.Knockout for QuestionType.YesNo, decimal? Question.Min and decimal? Question.Max
for QuestionType.Number, int? Question.MaxLength for the text types and
IReadOnlyList<string>? Question.AcceptedFileTypes for QuestionType.File.

Questionnaire.description: The screening questions a candidate answers when applying.

RuleResult.description: One rule's result, so an audit or a simulation shows which conditions held.

SalaryRequest.description: A pay range. Currency and period may come from the template's posting defaults on create.

SignInMethods.description: How a person can sign in here: the configured identity providers, and whether email links work.

SignInProvider.description: An identity provider button on the sign-in page.

SimulatedAutomation.description: What one automation would do. Only automations the trigger fires are listed, in definition order.

SimulateWorkflowRequest.description:
"Test this workflow" (workflow-engine.md §4): run a sample application through a workflow and see which automations
a trigger would fire. Nothing is saved or sent. `facts` is the sample application's snapshot; leave members out
for facts it does not have.

UpdateJobRequest.description: Replaces a job's posting content. A published job keeps its slug; a closed job cannot change.

ValidateWorkflowRequest.description: A workflow to check, as the builder holds it before saving.

WorkflowChange.description: One difference between two workflows. `before` and `after` are values, or JSON for objects and lists.

WorkflowStage.description: One step of the pipeline. `hired`, `rejected` and `withdrawn` are terminal.

WorkflowValidationResult.description:
The validator's verdict, guardrails included. 200 either way: a workflow with problems is a normal answer here, and
each problem has a JSON path such as `automations[0].actions[0]` the builder can point at.
